newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: U.N. envoy said meeting Cyprus leaders separately.
newsitem.headline: U.N. envoy said meeting Cyprus leaders separately.

text.p: The U.N. official chairing talks on the Cyprus problem scheduled separate meetings on Thursday with leaders of the Greek and Turkish Cypriot communities, with the possibility of a joint meeting later, an informed source said.

The talks, involving President Glafcos Clerides and Turkish Cypriot leader Rauf Denktash, aim to revive negotiations on reuniting the divided island as a bi-zonal, bi-communal federation. The United Nations has clamped a news blackout on the negotiations.

When Secretary-General Kofi Annan opened the five days of talks on Wednesday at a rural resort called Troutbeck, north of New York City, he said his special adviser for Cyprus, former Ecuadorean Foreign Minister Diego Cordovez, would submit "a number of suggestions" to the two sides.

The source said it was possible Cordovez would float the suggestions at separate 90-minute meetings scheduled first with Clerides and then with Denktash. They were likely to be followed by a joint meeting and then possibly a meeting just between the two Cypriot leaders.
A meeting on Wednesday afternoon in which all three took part was said to have been devoted largely to procedural matters.

The source said no decision had yet been made regarding another round of talks, although there have been persistent reports one was likely to be held at a location near Geneva during the first half of August.
Cyprus has been virtually partitioned since troops from Turkey took over the north of the island in 1974 in reaction to a coup in Nicosia backed by the junta then ruling Greece.

But the two communities have been at loggerheads since 1963, three years after independence from Britain, when a government in which both took part broke apart amid violence that resulted in the dispatch of a U.N. peacekeeping force still stationed on the island.
